scholarships.title: Embassy Science Fellowship (ESF-NL) 2027
scholarships.official_source: Dutch Research Council (NWO) and Ministry of Foreign Affairs

existing.description: This Call for proposals is open to all PhD graduates at any of the following research organisations and to 'lectoren' and senior researchers of universities of applied sciences:
eligibility: Be a PhD graduate at a listed research organisation: a Dutch university or university of applied sciences, a university medical centre, a KNAW or NWO institute, the Netherlands Cancer Institute, the Max Planck Institute for Psycholinguistics, Naturalis Biodiversity Center, ARCNL, the Princess Máxima Center, IHE Delft Institute for Water Education, or a TO2 institution
Be a 'lecten' or senior researcher at a university of applied sciences
Have an employment contract running at least until the end of the fellowship period
Researchers who have not yet obtained their PhD but whose PhD date is fixed may apply, provided the degree is obtained at the start of the fellowship
Apply for no more than one of the 12 selected positions
Be available during the fellowship period of 1 March 2027 to 29 February 2028
existing.eligibility_summary: PhD graduates at a listed Dutch research organisation, and 'lectoren' and senior researchers at universities of applied sciences, whose contract runs at least until the end of the fellowship period. Researchers whose PhD date is fixed but who have not yet obtained the degree may submit, provided they hold the degree at the start of the fellowship. Applicants may apply for a maximum of one of the 12 mission positions.
benefits: Grant of up to EUR 30,000 for the fellowship
Funding for international travel in economy class
Funding for research expenses, including domestic travel, representation and meetings
Replacement grant to cover the applicant's work at home
The host mission helps with accommodation and a place to work
Practical experience in a diplomatic context and a contribution to Dutch foreign policy
coverage: International travel expenses for economy class air travel or train fares
Research expenses, including domestic travel, representation expenses and costs for meetings
requirements: Submit the complete application in the Isaac application and reporting system
Create an Isaac account at least one workday in advance if you do not have one
Use the current budget form: on 12-08-2026 the budget form was replaced with a new version
State in the motivation letter which fellowship you are interested in, why you are suitable, what value you bring, and your availability between 1 March 2027 and 29 February 2028
State your approach to involving relevant local partners and stakeholders in the research
Do not mention h-indexes, journal impact factors or any other indicator of general journal or publisher reputation
Submit before the deadline, since late proposals will not be considered
documents: Motivation letter in PDF, maximum 2 x A4 in Calibri font size 10 with normal margins and single line spacing, including a provisional working plan
Narrative CV in PDF, maximum 500 words
Key outputs in PDF, maximum 5 items, with one hyperlink per item
Budget form in Excel using the standard format provided
Signed statement by the main applicant, as required in Isaac
existing.english_requirement: The proposal is written in English.
application_method: Register or create an Isaac account at least one workday in advance
Download the current forms from Isaac and use them
Write the motivation letter, narrative CV, key outputs and budget form
Upload all mandatory annexes to the proposal in Isaac
existing.selection_notes: Proposals are assessed against three weighted criteria: quality and motivation of the applicant (40%), match between the applicant and the assignment as formulated by the mission (40%), and feasibility (20%). Because of the expertise on the assessment committee and the small size of the grant, NWO applies Article 2.2.4 second subsection of the NWO Grant Rules 2024 and assesses proposals without involving referees. The assessment consists of an assessment committee meeting in October 2026 and decision-making by the NWO Executive Board in November 2026.
existing.best_fit: Researchers at a Dutch research institution whose scientific expertise matches a specific mission's project description, who can be seconded abroad for 1 to 3 months between 1 March 2027 and 29 February 2028 and whose contract runs to the end of that period.
existing.notes: Twelve researchers are placed per year, at missions in Australia, Canada, Chile, Egypt, Ivory Coast, Malaysia, the Permanent Representation in Rome, Senegal, South Africa, South Korea, Taiwan and Vietnam. The mission helps fellows find accommodation and a place to work. The programme aims to strengthen the interaction between diplomacy and science, with fellows applying their scientific expertise and international networks to inform evidence-informed Dutch foreign policy. Note an internal discrepancy on NWO's own page: the body text states 'The available budget for this Call for proposals is €390,000' while the Characteristics block states 'Budget €360,000'.
existing.duration: 1 to 3 months of secondment to a Dutch diplomatic mission, within the fellowship period 1 March 2027 to 29 February 2028
existing.application_period: 2027 cycle: informative webinar 2 July 2026, proposal deadline 10 September 2026 14:00 CEST, decision by November 2026, fellowship period 1 March 2027 to 29 February 2028
existing.deadline_display: 10 September 2026 before 14:00:00 CEST - Deadline for proposals. Proposals submitted after the deadline will not be taken into consideration by NWO.
existing.program_type: Government-funded research secondment fellowship placing researchers at Dutch diplomatic missions abroad

scholarships.title: KITLV Visiting Fellowship
scholarships.official_source: Royal Netherlands Institute of Southeast Asian and Caribbean Studies (KITLV)

existing.description: The KITLV Visiting Fellowship is a three month funded research stay at the Royal Netherlands Institute of Southeast Asian and Caribbean Studies (KITLV) in Leiden for researchers who hold a PhD in the social sciences and/or humanities and are not tax residents of the Netherlands. Fellows work on a publication or research project of their own choice in Southeast Asian or Caribbean Studies and do not need a university or research institute affiliation. The offer covers a return economy air or train fare, reimbursement of accommodation costs in Leiden up to EUR 2,000 per month against proof of payment, and a case-by-case monthly compensation for higher living costs. It is explicitly not a salaried position and fellows are expected to have a steady income during the stay.
eligibility: Have a PhD in the Social Sciences and/or Humanities
Carry out research in the field(s) of Southeast Asian and/or Caribbean Studies
Are interested to carry out their desired research in the Netherlands
Are prepared to be based at KITLV during the entire period of the fellowship
Are not a (tax) resident of The Netherlands
Have a steady income for the period of the Visiting Fellowship
No affiliation at a university or research institute is required
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants must hold a PhD in the social sciences and/or humanities, carry out research in Southeast Asian and/or Caribbean Studies, wish to conduct that research in the Netherlands, be prepared to be based at KITLV for the entire fellowship period, and not be a (tax) resident of the Netherlands. No university or research institute affiliation is required, but fellows must have a steady income during the fellowship.
benefits: Return economy air or train fare
Accommodation in Leiden reimbursed up to EUR 2,000 per month
Formal invitation letter and residence permit support
coverage: Return air or train fare (economy class) to and from the Netherlands
Reimbursement of accommodation costs in Leiden including rent, energy costs and applicable service costs, up to EUR 2,000 per month, based on proof of payment
Monthly compensation for higher living costs in Leiden compared with the main place of residence, calculated case by case
Formal letter of invitation and support in applying for a residence permit if needed
requirements: Candidates are invited to send in a proposal of the work they wish to carry out while at KITLV.
existing.english_requirement: Applications must be submitted in English.
application_method: Submit the application form and two-page CV via the official online application route
Do not email the application to the Program Chair; the page states 'do not email him your application'
existing.selection_notes: Selection is based on the submitted application documents only and no interviews are held. Applications are assessed by a rotating committee composed of KITLV staff. For the 2026 call KITLV aimed to inform all applicants by the end of April. Note: KITLV states it will not review any proposals before submission and/or the deadline.
existing.best_fit: PhD holders in the humanities and social sciences researching Southeast Asian or Caribbean Studies who are not tax residents of the Netherlands and can maintain their own steady income for three months.
existing.notes: KITLV is an institute of the Royal Netherlands Academy of Arts and Sciences (KNAW) and works closely with Leiden University. KITLV does not assist in finding accommodation - that is the fellow's own responsibility. Selection takes place twice a year, so there is a second annual window even if the current call closes.
existing.application_period: Open Call, selection twice a year. Eight three-month fellowships are available each year across four periods: March-May, June-August, September-November and December-February. The next call is published in September 2026 and closes 14 October 2026.
existing.deadline_display: The stored 2026 (2nd) call closed at "21 March 2026, midnight (CET)". The next still-applicable deadline published by KITLV is: "If you are interested and eligible, please apply at the latest on 14 October 2026." Selection for the annual programme takes place twice a year via an Open Call.
existing.program_type: Funded visiting research fellowship (three month research stay)
